author: golden state today
title: California beach volleyball hosts Battle of the Bay for home opener
text:
The No. 10-ranked California beach volleyball team is set to begin its 2026 home season by hosting the Battle of the Bay at Clark Kerr Sand Courts in Berkeley. The Golden Bears, who hold a 1-4 record, will face Sac State and UC Davis on Friday, followed by matches against USF and Pacific on Saturday.
Last weekend, the Bears competed at the Outrigger DUKE Kahahamoku Beach Classic in Honolulu. They recorded one win and four losses, with each defeat coming against top-10 ranked teams and all ending with a close score of 3-2. Cal secured a victory over No. 16 Hawai’i with a 3-0 result. The team dropped just one spot in this week’s AVCA rankings after being ranked No. 9 in the preseason poll.
Junior Emma Donley and senior Portia Sherman received recognition as the AVCA/CBVB National Pair of the Week after going undefeated (4-0) against top-10 opponents. “Donley and Sherman dropped just one set over the four matches,” according to the release. The pair previously made program history as Cal’s first AVCA First-Team All-Americans last season.
Another notable performance came from junior Ava Haughy, a transfer from Arizona State, who debuted for Cal last weekend. Teaming up with Gia Fisher—a 2025 All-MPSF selection—Haughy helped secure four wins out of five matches in Honolulu, including victories over pairs from Stanford, USC, Loyola Marymount, and Hawai’i.
Looking ahead, Cal plans to move into a new facility—the Banatao Family Beach Volleyball Stadium—in 2027. This project is supported by an $8 million fundraising effort through Cal’s Gender Equity Campaign and is part of ongoing efforts to comply with Title IX regulations established in 1972 that prohibit sex discrimination in educational programs receiving financial aid.
Head Coach Meagan Owusu leads Cal for her tenth season. Under her guidance, the team has qualified for each of the past four NCAA Championships and finished within the top twelve nationally for eight consecutive years—including four straight seasons ending in the top ten. Owusu also played as a defensive specialist for Cal’s indoor volleyball program from 2007 to 2010.
For continued updates on Cal beach volleyball, fans can follow @calbeachvb on Instagram and X.
